transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I keep eating in the evenings until I’m so full it’s uncomfortable, even when I don’t really want more. Some folks at my church group encouraged me to come in and talk to someone about it because it's really been weighing on me.
During these episodes, do you feel a sense of loss of control over your eating, such as feeling unable to stop or refrain from eating once you have started?

Yes, I feel a complete loss of control once I start. It feels like something else takes over and I'm just watching myself grab one thing after another from the kitchen. Even when I'm telling myself to stop, I just can't seem to do it until everything is gone or I'm in physical discomfort.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever engage in behaviors like self-induced vomiting, excessive exercise, or the use of laxatives to try to undo what you have eaten?

No, I don't do any of those things. I've never tried to make myself throw up, over-exercise, or use laxatives after I eat like that. I usually just end up sitting there in my recliner feeling miserable.
How many days per week, on average, would you say these episodes of eating occur, and how long has this pattern been happening?

It's been happening pretty much every night, at least several times a week. This has been going on for about three months now, starting right around when my divorce was finalized and I transitioned off the road.
Do you experience significant feelings of guilt, shame, or distress specifically regarding these eating episodes, rather than just feeling physically uncomfortable?

Yes, I feel terrible afterward. I'll sit there in the quiet house staring at the empty containers, feeling gross and deeply ashamed of myself. It’s embarrassing that a grown man who used to manage tight delivery schedules can’t even control what he puts in his own mouth.
